Battle of Hat Dich.fact: At 14:38 a section patrol from 2 Platoon W Company 4 RAR/NZ clashing with five VC at 10 metres (33 ft) while conducting a reconnaissance of a track, killing two and capturing an AK-47 and a pistol. Battle of Hat Dich.fact: On 15 February 10 Platoon D Company had deployed to southern end of the battalion AO to mount a night ambush on a high bank on a sharp bend in the Suoi Cau river.

Battle of Hat Dich.fact: At least two sampans were sunk and six VC killed before they were able to withdraw to the southern bank and engage the Australians with small arms and RPGs. Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping

Battle of Hat Dich.fact: B and W Companies 4 RAR/NZ, each accompanied by a tracker team and a Centurion tank troop from B Squadron, 1st Armoured Regiment were subsequently tasked to patrol to the area by separate routes.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Well concealed in bunkers the defenders successfully initiated a command-detonated directional mine and opened fire with small-arms and RPGs, killing one _____ and wounding five others
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: On 16 February, just prior to a ceasefire for the Tết New Year festival, the Australian command had received information from an agent about the location of large weapon caches in the north of AO Tiki, and a large VC force was also expected to be in position. Well concealed in bunkers the defenders successfully initiated a command-detonated directional mine and opened fire with small-arms and RPGs, killing one Australian and wounding five others.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: The remainder of the casualties were then moved by helicopter to the _____ at Vung Tau
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: The remainder of the casualties were then moved by helicopter to the Australian Field Hospital at Vung Tau.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping

Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Lacking the medium artillery and air strikes required to successfully assault the fortified position, B Company withdrew to a safe distance and kept the position under observation and fire.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: A follow-up attack schedule for the next day was also cancelled due to the unavailability of _____ artillery
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Circling overhead in another Sioux helicopter Greville protested, and although Pearson had supported him the Americans refused to provide offensive support despite the contact having been initiated by the VC. A follow-up attack schedule for the next day was also cancelled due to the unavailability of American artillery.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: During the night a large VC force was observed withdrawing, with one party of about 30 men passing close to a concealed _____; frustrated, the Australians observed the truce and held their fire
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: During the night a large VC force was observed withdrawing, with one party of about 30 men passing close to a concealed Centurion; frustrated, the Australians observed the truce and held their fire.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: A thorough search of the area by the _____ was not possible however, and B Company was ordered to return to their patrol area to prepare for redeployment
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Although there were numerous signs of casualties, with a large number of blood trails and some damaged weapons the Australians found only three dead, with the VC once again having cleared the battlefield of the dead and wounded during the night. Later intelligence suggested that the position had been occupied by the headquarters of the 274th Regiment and one of its battalions and the Australians considered it likely that the VC battalion had fought a delaying action to allow the headquarters ...

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: The fighting had been one of the more significant actions of _____ and for his leadership during this action Reynolds was awarded the Military Cross
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: The fighting had been one of the more significant actions of Operation Goodwood and for his leadership during this action Reynolds was awarded the Military Cross.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping

Battle of Hat Dich.fact: At 01:45 on 18 February a sentry from D Company had detected noise and movement to the south, just outside the wire.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping

Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Estimated at up to company strength, the VC were observed clearly through a Starlight scope and were moving noisily, likely unaware of their proximity to the fire support base.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping

Battle of Hat Dich.question: FSB _____ closed and HQ 1 ATF moved to FSB Kerry in preparation for upcoming operations
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: FSB Julia closed and HQ 1 ATF moved to FSB Kerry in preparation for upcoming operations.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Throughout the operation the bulk of the contacts had been initiated by the _____, a reverse of the American trend in which more than two-thirds of actions were normally initiated by the VC
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Throughout the operation the bulk of the contacts had been initiated by the Australians, a reverse of the American trend in which more than two-thirds of actions were normally initiated by the VC. Although there were few major actions, the operation was considered a success by the Australians and following it VC activity in 1 ATFs area of operations visibly lessened as the VC were forced to abandon their permanent bases in the Hat Dich and disrupting their preparations for upcoming offensive ...

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: From _____ most operations tended to be platoon and company-sized, and confined to Phước Tuy
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: From 1969 most operations tended to be platoon and company-sized, and confined to Phước Tuy.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: There was little respite for the _____ though, with both 4 RAR/NZ and 9 RAR immediately redeploying in anticipation of another PAVN/VC offensive during Tet, under Operation Federal
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Operation Goodwood was one of the longest out of province operations mounted by the Australians during the war and was also the last Australian multi-battalion operation to be fought across the border with third-country forces. It had been a period of intense activity for the Australians and the Royal Australian Regiment, the 3rd Cavalry Regiment and 1st Armoured Regiment were subsequently awarded the battle honour "Hat Dich", one of only five presented to Australian units during the war.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: 1 RAR subsequently returned to Australia after being relieved by 5 RAR—under the command of _____—on 15 February
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: 1 RAR subsequently returned to Australia after being relieved by 5 RAR—under the command of Lieutenant Colonel Colin Kahn—on 15 February.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Arriving in Sydney on 28 February _____, 1 RAR was welcomed home with a march through the city
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: This operation in late-February 1969 saw 1 ATF—less one battalion and other elements required to secure its base in Nui Dat—once again operating outside Phước Tuy Province to secure the major bases of Long Binh, Biên Hòa and the capital Saigon from an impending offensive. Arriving in Sydney on 28 February 1969, 1 RAR was welcomed home with a march through the city.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: During the tour—its second in South Vietnam—the battalion had killed at least _____ VC and destroyed a large number of bunkers, camps, and caches and had been heavily involved in the Battle of Coral–B
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: During the tour—its second in South Vietnam—the battalion had killed at least 276 VC and destroyed a large number of bunkers, camps, and caches and had been heavily involved in the Battle of Coral–Balmoral.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: The _____ Tet offensive began in the early hours of 23 February, with PAVN/VC attacks against US and ARVN installations and district capitals
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Arriving in Sydney on 28 February 1969, 1 RAR was welcomed home with a march through the city. The 1969 Tet offensive began in the early hours of 23 February, with PAVN/VC attacks against US and ARVN installations and district capitals.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Lacking the ferocity of the _____ Tet Offensive, the outburst soon slackened, however
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Lacking the ferocity of the 1968 Tet Offensive, the outburst soon slackened, however.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: In III CTZ, where 1 ATF operated, over a period of five days there were 175 attacks by fire and just 15 ground assaults, while the _____/VC suffered over 1,800 killed and 320 captured
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: The 1969 Tet offensive began in the early hours of 23 February, with PAVN/VC attacks against US and ARVN installations and district capitals. In III CTZ, where 1 ATF operated, over a period of five days there were 175 attacks by fire and just 15 ground assaults, while the PAVN/VC suffered over 1,800 killed and 320 captured.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Although _____ forces were by now operating in these areas, VC guerrilla groups operated with freedom, especially at night
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Although ARVN forces were by now operating in these areas, VC guerrilla groups operated with freedom, especially at night.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: As a consequence Australian operations in mid-_____ were forced to focus on the area around Dat Do and the Long Hải Hills, as they attempted to restrict the VC's access to the local population
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Regardless, with the bulk of 1 ATF operating away from Nui Dat in first half of 1969, the VC again became active in the populated central and southern areas of Phước Tuy Province, including Dat Do and Long Dien and the villages between Dat Do and the coast. As a consequence Australian operations in mid-1969 were forced to focus on the area around Dat Do and the Long Hải Hills, as they attempted to restrict the VC's access to the local population.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: An assault by the _____ platoon pushed the VC out of the bunkers and they secured the area after following the withdrawing force 200 metres (220 yd) to the south-west
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: At 17:00 7 Platoon contacted 14 VC armed with AK-47 assault rifles on the edge of a clearing, killing one while the others withdrew to a bunker system and engaged the Australians with small arms and 60 mm mortars. An assault by the Australian platoon pushed the VC out of the bunkers and they secured the area after following the withdrawing force 200 metres (220 yd) to the south-west.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: More than 1,000 metres (1,100 yd) away, Honner moved quickly to bring the remainder of C _____ to the aid of the platoon in contact
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: That morning in AO Wondai, 1 Platoon A Company 1 RAR was watching the northern bank of Suoi Cau Moi and at 07:45 they contacted three VC as they attempted to cross the creek, killing one. Thirty minutes later 7 Platoon, C Company had been engaged by two VC while moving into a new ambush location.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Meanwhile, a number of SAS patrols were inserted by air and road on 6 _____ 1969 to gather information on PAVN/VC troop movements
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Meanwhile, a number of SAS patrols were inserted by air and road on 6 January 1969 to gather information on PAVN/VC troop movements. Further patrols were deployed to the southern Biên Hòa-Firestone Trail area in mid-January, while additional SAS patrols were inserted on 29 January in an attempt to ascertain PAVN/VC troop movements.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: On 13 _____ moved to establish FSB Margaret 1 kilometre (0.62 mi) east of Tam Phuoc in Biên Hòa Province, located in AO Kilcoy immediately west of AO Wondai
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: On 13 January Bennett moved to establish FSB Margaret 1 kilometre (0.62 mi) east of Tam Phuoc in Biên Hòa Province, in AO Kilcoy immediately west of AO Wondai.

Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Around 10:30 four VC approached 8 Platoon and were engaged with small arms; returning fire with RPGs which slightly wounded three Australians, three VC were then killed while a sweep by the Australians failed to locate the fourth.
